decision: Lead with the closest full Moon of 2026 (24 Dec, 356,729 km) and use Moon-Jupiter on 27 Dec as the single secondary; skip the Ursids and the planetary scan
rationale: The full Moon is the only event in the window with a superlative a viewer can verify by looking: it is 13.8% wider than the year's farthest full Moon, and it is high in the south at midnight. Moon-Jupiter at 2.1 deg is a bright naked-eye pairing at 52 deg altitude before dawn. The Ursids are ZHR 10 and would dilute a 30 s cut; Venus at 21 deg altitude is a weaker repeat of last week.
alternatives: Make the Ursids the lead (rejected: ZHR 10, and the Moon is 82% lit the same night)
Two-event short without the full Moon (rejected: misses the Christmas hook)
